scope: Independent read-only source review of the five frozen QA URL-tracer paths and one execution of the new 23-case file. No production source, provider, authentication, workflow/ref, deadline or acceptance changes by this reviewer.

scopeVerification.iosRunnerDiff: Exactly one helper invocation after successful Expo prebuild and before plist preparation/CocoaPods. Removing that line restores the published b5 runner byte for byte.

conclusion.acceptedPurpose: Observe entry to and return from the generated QA AppDelegate open-URL method, so a later native run can compare that boundary with the existing JS received/parsed/action/mounted/readback markers.
conclusion.noCausalClaim: No native URL-delivery timing or cause of the prior b5 delay is established by these local source/fixture tests.

reviewFindings.finding: The helper requires one exact AppDelegate class anchor, one exact open-URL method/signature and one original forwarding line. It inserts the observation before the unchanged return expression: super.application(...) || RCTLinkingManager.application(...). Operand order, short-circuit evaluation and returned Bool are byte-preserved. Removing only added observer/import text exactly restores the entire original generated source.

The entry marker precedes original forwarding. Swift defer emits the exit marker on return from that method; it does not await JS event handling, rewrite the URL, choose a different handler, schedule work, sleep, retry or call forwarding twice.

Only the exact QA bundle and QA scheme qualify. A per-delegate counter admits at most 16 qualifying calls, producing at most 32 intended records. Log arguments are sequence, Foundation epoch milliseconds and a numeric exact-fixture-match flag; URL text, query/options, tokens, session data and environment values are not logged. The URL is inspected solely to compute the match Boolean.

The helper requires CI=true, app environment qa and the fixed synthetic transport-key sentinel. It accepts no path arguments. The fixed original-source manifest must bind the current nonempty GITHUB_SHA and GITHUB_RUN_ID and the exact helper SHA. Wrong/missing run, commit, helper hash, manifest shape, imports, method, forwarding or duplicate observer fail before generated-source mutation.

Source/helper reads are capped at 128 KiB and the manifest at 1 MiB. Preexisting symlinks are rejected, regular files checked, and evidence reuse refused. The fixed generated QA AppDelegate is replaced through an exclusive temporary file only after full before/after source copies have been retained. This is controlled CI preparation, not a general adversarial-filesystem API.

The separate source-proof records current commit/run, helper and original-manifest hashes, full before/after hashes and sizes, the forwarding-expression hash, exact reversal, log bounds/fields and uncalibrated clock. Generated Swift is retained as .swift.txt. The new helper is included in original-source provenance before prebuild; existing six source overlays remain distinct.

The real shell under controlled tool fixtures reaches CocoaPods only after a valid patch. A changed method exits 2 before CocoaPods, while valid preparation preserves the injected pod failure exit 31. Existing compiler/signing/flow/media-decoder/verifier/status/cleanup logic and native acceptance deadlines are unchanged.

The tests execute the actual Python patcher against the installed Expo template, that template after the repository VoIP config-plugin AppDelegate callback, and an existing Foundation import. They restore and compare the entire original source, not only the forwarding line. The plugin dangerous filesystem mod and native build/provider programs are controlled test doubles.

independentExecution.mode: approved subprocess-enabled local execution; real patcher and shell, temporary fixtures and stubbed provider/build programs

limits: No Swift compiler, UIKit/Expo runtime, iPhone Simulator, physical device or native log stream was executed here. The next native CI build must confirm compilation and actual log delivery.
The 16-call/32-record contract is verified from emitted Swift and assumes normal serialized AppDelegate delivery. This is not an adversarial concurrent-caller stress test.
NSLog and Date observation add work. These markers diagnose ordering and boundary delay; they do not establish uninstrumented performance.
Foundation Date uses wall-clock epoch milliseconds, not a monotonic clock calibrated against Maestro, host logs or JS timestamps. Cross-clock differences require explicit qualification.
An exit marker establishes only return from the delegate method. It does not establish which short-circuit branch handled the URL or downstream JS/React completion.

Missing markers can reflect unobserved process/log coverage, exhausted bounded trace budget, a nonmatching scheme/bundle or no delegate call. Missing logs alone do not prove the operating system never delivered the URL.
File checks reject the tested preexisting symlinks and oversized inputs; no concurrent filesystem-race or hardlink-adversary guarantee is claimed for the trusted disposable checkout.
The original-source hash guard is preparation provenance, not a final signed-binary attestation. Actual generated before/after proof must be inspected from the future artifact.
